_comment: A reconstruction of the case owner testing reported: a senior AI-quality career
base scanned against an ENTRY-LEVEL data-annotation posting, which returned Gap
on every requirement. The resume is the repo's fictional persona (SPEC v1.2) —
synthetic data, the same persona tests/e2e already carries. The posting is
written around the phrases the owner quoted from theirs ('quality checks',
'quality standards', 'label, categorize', '0-2 years of experience in data
entry, data annotation, or similar role'), so both findings of that round —
the non-literal keywords and the threshold calibration — are reproducible from
resumeText:
MIRA STEINBERG
AI Quality Analyst — Hamburg, Germany

SUMMARY
Four years in AI data quality: LLM output evaluation, annotation quality
assurance, and the Python tooling around both.

EXPERIENCE

AI Prompt Evaluator — Nordlicht Digital (01/2025 – present)
Evaluated and annotated Russian and English LLM outputs against scoring rubrics,
including prompt-response pairs and multi-turn dialogues.
Performed side-by-side evaluation and ranking of model responses for a weekly
release review, at roughly 400 items per week.
Maintained an average QA quality score of 98 percent across all batches.
Wrote the annotation guidelines the rest of the team worked from, and ran the
calibration sessions that kept inter-annotator agreement above 0.85.

Data Quality Specialist — BotWorks Labs (05/2024 – 12/2024)
Reviewed and corrected labelled training data for an intent-classification
model: audited sampled batches, tracked error rates per annotator, and fed the
findings back into the guidelines.
Built Python pipelines that de-duplicated incoming datasets, validated schema
conformance and produced the weekly quality report.
Worked to a documented turnaround target and hit it in 11 of 12 months.

Business Analyst — BotWorks Labs (05/2023 – 04/2024)
Mapped as-is and to-be procurement processes in BPMN for three client programmes
and ran requirements workshops with up to twelve stakeholders.
Documented forty user stories with acceptance criteria for a warehouse
management rollout.

SKILLS
LLM evaluation, annotation quality assurance, inter-annotator agreement,
guideline authoring, Python (pandas), SQL, spreadsheets, BPMN process modeling,
requirements documentation. English C1, Russian native, German B2.

EDUCATION
BSc Business Informatics — Universitaet Hamburg (2016 – 2020)
vacancyText:
Data Annotator (Entry Level) — Helle Daten GmbH, Berlin (remote)

We are building training datasets for computer-vision and language models, and
we are looking for a Data Annotator to join our operations team. This is an
entry-level role: we train you on the tools.

What you will do:
- Label, categorize and tag images, short texts and audio clips according to our
  written annotation guidelines.
- Run quality checks on your own batches before submitting them, and fix the
  items that do not meet our quality standards.
- Flag unclear cases to the project lead instead of guessing.
- Keep to the agreed daily throughput without letting accuracy slip.
- Take part in weekly calibration meetings with the rest of the annotation team.

What you need:
- 0-2 years of experience in data entry, data annotation, or similar role.
- Attention to detail and patience for repetitive work.
- Good written English; a second language is welcome.
- Comfortable working with spreadsheets and simple web tools.
- Reliable home internet for remote work, and a quiet place to work.

Nice to have:
- Experience with annotation platforms such as Label Studio or CVAT.
- Basic Python for small data clean-up tasks.

We offer a permanent contract, 28 days of holiday, a remote-first setup and paid
training. Remote within Germany; we meet in Berlin twice a year.
